turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. Well, I'm here because I just can't stop thinking about my appearance. It's my hairline, mostly, and... and just the way my face looks. I work as a host at a restaurant, and under those lights there, I just feel like I look really old and strange. 

It's on my mind all the time. The people I work with tell me they don't see what I'm talking about, but I know what I see, and I just can't seem to get past it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes a constant preoccupation with their hairline and face looking 'old and strange', which their coworkers do not observe.

turns.doctor_question: Because of these worries about your appearance, do you find yourself repeatedly doing things like checking in mirrors, fixing your hair, or trying to hide your face?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. A lot, actually. Especially right before a shift. I'll just keep checking the bathroom mirror over and over. I even take pictures on my phone from different angles to see how bad it looks, and... and I keep combing my hair forward to try and cover it up. 

I just get stuck replaying how the guests are going to see me when they walk in. It gets to the point where I end up running late, or I just get too worked up to even go out to the front of the restaurant.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors such as repeatedly checking mirrors, taking photos from different angles, and combing their hair forward to cover up perceived flaws.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from worries about your appearance, do you have other repetitive thoughts or habits that you feel compelled to do, such as repeatedly checking locks, excessive cleaning, or arranging things in a specific way?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I make sure the door is locked when I leave the house, like anyone else, but it's not something I get stuck on. I don't have to go back and check it over and over or anything like that. It's really just... just the stuff with my hair and my face that takes up all my time and energy. I don't really have any habits with cleaning or organizing things.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient notes that concerns about their hair and face take up all their time and energy, confirming a preoccupation with physical appearance.
symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient denies having other repetitive thoughts or getting 'stuck' on things outside of their appearance concerns.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly denies having compulsive habits like repeatedly checking locks, excessive cleaning, or organizing things.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever think that your perception of your appearance might be exaggerated, or are you completely convinced that your hairline and face look as bad as you think?
turns.patient_response:
I'm not really sure. I mean, I guess because my coworkers tell me they don't see it, part of me wonders if... if maybe I'm making it worse in my head. 

But when I actually look in the mirror, it's just so obvious to me. I see exactly how bad it is. So, most of the time, yeah, I'm completely convinced it looks as awful as I think it does. I just can't see it any other way.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes being convinced of how awful their hairline and face look, despite acknowledging that coworkers do not see the perceived defects.
